title: The Serum Run

slides.title: A TOWN WAS IN DANGER. ONLY DOGS COULD SAVE IT.

slides.text: January 1925. Nome, Alaska. A deadly disease called diphtheria starts spreading among the town's children.
The medicine that can stop it is about 1,085 km (674 miles) away, at the end of a railway line.
Ships can't get through the sea ice. The few planes in Alaska are packed away for winter, and flying in that cold is judged too risky. So they choose dogs.
The plan: a relay. 20 mushers and about 150 sled dogs, passing a 9 kg (20 lb) package of medicine from team to team.
Temperatures fell to around -46°C (-50°F). Winds could freeze skin in minutes. And every hour counted.

One team would take the most dangerous stretch of all: straight across a frozen sea that could crack beneath them. Their lead dog was 12 years old.
Part 2: Togo.
